note: Window agent p1300-p1399, 1 Nov 2026. Southern Manchuria (Naghachu) held by the Northern Yuan from 1375 and by the Ming only after the 1387-88 campaign (events/0-1, keyframe_overrides/0-1 and 7); Khwarezm kept Timurid after 1388 (keyframe_overrides/2-3, rulings/0); the House of Ascania's keyframes of 1307-1388 repaired for the unresolvable place 'Lauenburg' (keyframe_overrides/8-16); Kutai Kartanegara's 1300 shape (keyframe_overrides/4), Azcapotzalco's Colhuacan (events/3, keyframe_overrides/5) and Venice's Argos of 1394 (events/2, keyframe_overrides/6), which never resolved. Also the Yuan court's Inner Mongolian steppe and Koke Temur's Gansu in 1368-72 (events/4-5, keyframe_overrides/17). Pages silent, left as drawn: the Bahmani and Tughlaq Deccan of 1347-51, Ming land in Xinjiang and Heilongjiang before 1404-09, the Yuan remnant in Gansu 1368-71.

region.text: southern Manchuria, Naghachu's Liaoyang province: the Liaoning and Jilin land that the Ming dossier names as 'Naghachu's country' (ming-dynasty ledger/22)

events.note: 1375: Naghachu holds southern Manchuria for the Northern Yuan. Northern Yuan page: 'Naghachu, a Mongol official of Biligtu Khan in Liaoyang province, invaded Liaodong' in 1375, 'restoring Mongol power in China proper'; he 'continued to hold southern Manchuria' and 'eventually surrendered to the Ming dynasty' in 1387-88. Naghachu page: he 'had won hegemony over the Mongol tribes in a wide area including much of Rehe and Liaoning by the mid-1380s'. The draft leaves Liaoning and Jilin (about 1,880 cells) as nobody's land from the Yuan's fall in 1368 and then hands them to the Ming already at the 1385 keyframe, two years before the Ming campaign of 1387; the pages date Naghachu's role from 1375, so 1368-1374 is left as drawn (pages silent).

region.text: southern Manchuria, Naghachu's land (Liaoning and Jilin)

events.note: 1387-88: Naghachu surrenders and his land passes to the Ming. Northern Yuan page: 'Naghachu eventually surrendered to the Ming dynasty' (1387-88); Naghachu page: 'in 1387 the Ming sent a military campaign to attack Naghachu', which 'forced his surrender'. The Ming dossier's own gains (ledger/23 Jilin 1387, ledger/26 the Liaodong peninsula 1388) leave the rest of Liaoning (about 365 cells outside the peninsula) with the Northern Yuan until the Ming's 1402 keyframe; this event gives the whole of Naghachu's land to the Ming in 1388.

region.text: Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi, in the Argolid without the Corinth castellany disc that the Acciaioli keyframe of 1394 draws (the dossier's own place 'Argos' is not in the gazetteer, so its ledger/41 was skipped)

events.note: 11 June 1394: Lordship of Argos and Nauplia page: 'Argos was seized by the Despot Theodore I Palaiologos' and 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394, when he ceded them to Venice.' Replaces the skipped republic-of-venice ledger/41, whose place 'Argos' does not resolve; the Argolid region (7 cells) is wider than the three places, and the gain only takes the cells the Despotate of the Morea holds.

region.text: Colhuacan (Culhuacan), today the Iztapalapa borough of Mexico City; the gazetteer has no place 'Colhuacan', so the Mexico City admin-1 stands in (4 cells)

events.note: Colhuacan (altepetl) page: 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops' (the Colhuacan disambiguation page puts Pueblo Culhuacan in the Iztapalapa borough of Mexico City). The dossier's ledger/2 dates the conquest to 1385 from the Azcapotzalco page and was skipped because the place 'Colhuacan' does not resolve; the two pages differ (1377 and 1385), and this event takes the date of the page opened in this run. Only nobody's land passes. [Review p1300-p1399, 1 Nov 2026: corrected; the earlier note said the Mexica cells of Tenochtitlan stay its own, but since the Tlatelolco split of 1337 (tenochtitlan ledger/1) the one Mexico City cell that Azcapotzalco and Tenochtitlan share is nobody's, so the event moves all 4 Mexico City cells, Azcapotzalco's own city cell included.]

region.text: Shangdu and Yingchang with the steppe margin south of the Gobi that the Ming take in 1370: the same land as the Ming dossier's ledger/11 (Inner Mongolia inside Cliopatria's 1375 Ming outline)

events.note: September 1368: the Yuan court holds the Inner Mongolian steppe. Hongwu Emperor page: after Dadu fell 'The Yuan emperor Toghon Temur fled north to Shangdu'; in 1370 the Ming forced him 'to retreat further north to Yingchang, where he died later that month', and 'In June' Li Wenzhong took Yingchang. The draft hands the whole Yuan realm to nobody at the dissolution of September 1368 except the Mongolian core (the Northern Yuan's 1368 keyframe), so this steppe (3,590 cells) is nobody's from 1368 until the Ming 'gain from northern-yuan' of June 1370 (ming-dynasty ledger/11) takes it from no one; the extent is the Ming dossier's reading, the page names only the two cities.

January 1369: Hongwu Emperor page: Xu Da 'captured Taiyuan in January 1369, forcing Koke Temur to retreat to Gansu'; 'border skirmishes with Koke Temur's troops persisted until 1370'; in 1372 Feng Sheng 'was assigned to conquer the western part of the Gansu Corridor' (the Ming dossier's ledger/15 takes Gansu from the Northern Yuan in 1372). Until then the draft leaves Gansu (1,705 cells) as nobody's land from the Yuan's fall. The page does not mention Ningxia or Qinghai, which stay as drawn.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1385 shape without Liaoning and Jilin (Naghachu's land until his surrender in 1387-88) and without Heilongjiang (no Ming post before the Nurgan commission of 1409), plus the whole of Gansu and Ningxia as in the dossier's own correction

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1375 shape takes Liaoning and Jilin out ('they enter in the 1387-88 Manchurian campaign') but its 1385 shape (spanning 1385-1401) does not, so the draft gives the Ming 859 Liaoning and 681 Jilin cells from 1385, two years before the campaign. Northern Yuan page: Naghachu 'continued to hold southern Manchuria' and 'eventually surrendered to the Ming dynasty' in 1387-88. The Ming's own 1387-88 gains and events/1 bring the land in at the right date.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1375 Northern Yuan shape plus southern Manchuria (Liaoning and Jilin), Naghachu's Liaoyang province

keyframe_overrides.why: Northern Yuan page: in 1375 Naghachu, 'a Mongol official of Biligtu Khan in Liaoyang province', invaded Liaodong; he held southern Manchuria until he surrendered to the Ming in 1387-88. Cliopatria's 1375 Northern Yuan outline leaves Manchuria out, so without this the keyframe snap of 1375 would undo events/0.

correction.text: the 1385 Cliopatria shape with Fars and Kerman (the Muzaffarid lands) plus Isfahan, as the dossier has it, plus Khwarezm (taken from the Sufi dynasty in 1387-88)

keyframe_overrides.why: The draft gives the Timurids Khwarezm in 1388 (the Sufi dynasty's end hands its land over, 728 cells) and then the 1393 keyframe, cut from Cliopatria's 1385 outline, drops all 728 cells (Karakalpakstan 495, Tashauz 233) to nobody for 1393-94, with no event. Sufi dynasty page: 'Timur immediately took action against Suleiman Shah, overrunning Khwarezm and crushing the rebellion'; 'In the 15th century Khwarezm was usually controlled by the Timurids'; the Sufids stayed only 'as governors for the powers of the region' until 1505.

Same land, same page: Cliopatria's 1395 Timurid outline leaves Khwarezm out and its Golden Horde outline of 1395-1401 holds it (the golden-horde ledger/18 note says the page does not say Timur annexed it), so the draft draws Khwarezm as Golden Horde land from 1395. No event returns it to the Horde, the Sufi page says Khwarezm 'was usually controlled by the Timurids' in the 15th century, and Timur had overrun it in 1387-88. Keeps it Timurid with rulings/0. This shape spans 1395-1401; the years 1400-01 belong to the next window.

correction.text: Kutai Lama at the mouth of the Mahakam: a 20 km disc (the dossier's own radius) round the dossier's capital point for Kutai Lama (Tepian Batu), 117.2 E 0.55 S, 5 cells on the lower Mahakam below Samarinda; the gazetteer has no place 'Kutai Lama'

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's region {"place": "Kutai Lama", "km": 20} does not resolve, so the kingdom founded in 1300 owned no land. Sultanate page: 'the Hindu Kingdom of Martapura founded in 1300 at Kutai Lama', which lies 'at the mouth of the Mahakam River' (Anggana area). The page gives no coordinates, so the lower Mahakam round Samarinda stands in for the 20 km disc. This shape spans 1300-1634; the dossier's 1635 shape and ledger/1 carry the same unresolvable place (dossier request). [Review p1300-p1399, 1 Nov 2026: the earlier spec, the Mahakam within 55 km of Samarinda (12 cells), ran upstream past Tenggarong to 116.8 E, beside Muara Kaman, the capital of Kutai Martadipura (kutai-martadipura dossier), which the page has Kutai Kartanegara defeat only in 1635 ('In 1635, Kutai Kartanegara attacked and defeated Martapura'); the page puts the 1300 kingdom 'in the area of Kutai Lama at the mouth of the Mahakam River', so the shape is cut to the dossier's 20 km disc at its Kutai Lama point.]

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's region {"place": "Colhuacan", "km": 8} does not resolve, so the 1385-1413 shape never applied. Colhuacan page: 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan'; Pueblo Culhuacan is in the Iztapalapa borough of Mexico City. Same spec as events/3.

correction.text: the 1395 shape without Boeotia: Athens and Attica (and Megara), plus Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi, ceded to Venice on 11 June 1394

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own correction (1395 shape without Boeotia) lacks Argos, so the 1395 keyframe snap would take Argos away from Venice a year after the cession (Lordship page: 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394, when he ceded them to Venice'; the dossier's ledger/41 and Stato da Mar give Argos 1394-1462). Shape spans 1395-1401; later windows must carry Argos to 1462.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1375 shape without Liaoning and Jilin, which enter in the 1387-88 Manchurian campaign ('The campaign into Manchuria in 1387 was ultimately successful'); plus Sichuan without Kham ('By September 1371, Sichuan had been conquered'; Kham was Tibetan tribute land, Ming–Tibet relations page), all of Gansu ('Feng Sheng was assigned to conquer the western part of the Gansu Corridor', 1372) and Ningxia and Guizhou (bridged in 1374, confidence 1; Cliopatria's 1385 shape holds both), which Cliopatria's 1375 outline leaves partly out; and without Heilongjiang, where the Ming have no post before the Nurgan Regional Military Commission of 1409

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1375 Ming outline carries 150 cells of Heilongjiang (a block at 124-127.6 E, 44.7-46.3 N on the middle Songhua, cut off from the rest of Ming land) that no Ming event gives it and that the dossier's own 1415 shape treats as vassal land. Nurgan page: 'The seat was nominally established in 1409, but was abandoned in 1435'; the page names no Ming presence in the Amur-Heilongjiang region before 1409 (its earlier posts, at Boluohe, Nanghar and Wuliehe, were 'set up by the Yuan'). Also cut from the 1385 shape (keyframe_overrides/0). Hami (281 Xinjiang cells in the same outline) is left: the Kumul Khanate page gives no date for Ming rule there.
